about: Model-free inventory of every place a person is asked to confirm during a standard task (plan, implement, PR, review, merge), per agent kind and environment. It records what the code and docs say today and changes no behaviour. T1's templates/presets/autonomous.json and `ahub autonomy status` read it. A fact that could not be established is the word unknown, never a guess. Add a row for a new peer kind here (src/hub/confirmation-matrix.ts and test/confirmation-matrix.test.ts fail without one).

terminal.detect: No ORCA_WORKTREE_ID in the hub's environment and no Orca worktree on record for the project.
terminal.opens: A hub-made TUI start needs the machine-local terminal.open template. With none the start is refused with the command to run by hand, never downgraded to headless.

orca.detect: ORCA_WORKTREE_ID is set, or an earlier ahub <peer> launch of this project recorded an Orca worktree, and the orca executable is on PATH.
orca.opens: A hub-made TUI start runs `orca terminal create` in that worktree. A configured terminal.open template takes precedence.

headless.detect: No terminal: peers started with start_mode headless, the hub-native local worker, or a declared headless instance.
headless.opens: Nothing opens for the peer. A headless Kimi or Qwen start also opens an `ahub watch` pane through the provider when one exists, and the start stands without it.

claude.formNote: The kind itself has only a TUI. headless is a declared headless implementer instance (the Claude headless implementer, #525-4).

qwen.formNote: Headless ACP is the default. The TUI is explicit only (ahub qwen --mode tui, dual output) and the hub never opens it by itself.

permission_modes.<peer>.setBy: the person (a never-ask default also needs the console y at hub start)
permission_modes.<peer>.doc: docs/operations.md, Permission modes for running peers

permission.<peer>.where: the daemon's memory only (ahub permission <peer> <mode>, dashboard, ahub settings)
permission.<peer>.setBy: the person (never-ask needs the peer id typed or --yes plus the console y)
permission.<peer>.doc: docs/operations.md, Permission modes for running peers

action_policy.where: .agenthub/config.local.json only (enabled, always_ask, budgets). Shared config.json cannot set it.
action_policy.applies: live through the confirmed terminal reload
action_policy.default: enabled, always_ask is publish, external-write, destroy and install, budgets 1, 5, 3, 2
action_policy.setBy: the person (settings action_policy.enabled and action_policy.budgets.<class> are registered)

tasks.auto_pull.doc: docs/operations.md, Settings from the dashboard and the terminal

peers.<peer>.start_mode.doc: docs/operations.md, Start modes: TUI by default, headless as opt-in

terminal.open.where: .agenthub/config.local.json (an argv template with one {command} element). Not a setting: read at hub start.
terminal.open.default: none, so a hub-made TUI start uses Orca when it can, else is refused
terminal.open.doc: docs/operations.md, Start modes: TUI by default, headless as opt-in

pi.auto_start.applies: the next startup or recovery auto-start decision
pi.auto_start.doc: docs/operations.md, Settings from the dashboard and the terminal

launch.unattended.where: ahub up|daemon --unattended (hub level), ahub claude --unattended, ahub codex --unattended
launch.unattended.setBy: the person typing the launch command

release.authorize.where: ahub sdlc authorize-release <version> in a person's terminal, plus the managed pre-push tag guard
release.authorize.applies: per release, held in daemon memory only
release.authorize.setBy: the person alone (agents and delegated calls cannot)
release.authorize.doc: docs/operations.md, Release approval and optional tag guard

native.claude.where: Claude Code's own permission rules and settings, under ~/.claude or the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR home in use
native.claude.doc: docs/operations.md, Permission modes for running peers

native.codex.where: Codex's own approval policy and sandbox, under CODEX_HOME

native.kimi.where: Kimi's own TUI permission mode. The hub sets ACP default, yolo or auto only for its headless session.
native.kimi.doc: docs/operations.md, Kimi in its own TUI

native.qwen.where: Qwen's own approval mode. The dual-output TUI is launched with --approval-mode default.
native.qwen.doc: docs/operations.md, Qwen's own TUI, driven through dual output

native.jcode.where: Jcode's native policy. permission_modes.jcode is refused by the config loader.

native.agy.where: Antigravity's own TUI permission mode. --dangerously-skip-permissions and --unattended are refused by ahub agy.

unavailable.reason: Antigravity has no headless form. Headless and print starts are refused until their native mapping is verified.

rows.asks: Claude's own permission dialog for a write, edit, shell or other tool call in the person's terminal.
rows.note: In a managed launch (ahub claude) the PreToolUse hook sees every call. ask gives no hook decision, so Claude's own rules ask. ask-when-needed lets project file tools run outside .agenthub, .git and agent configuration. never-ask returns a hook allow for every tool. A session not started by ahub claude has no hub hook, and an --unattended launch skips every permission check, hooks included: the hub sees nothing there.

rows.asks: Claude's permission dialog for a publish, external-write, destroy or install call, returned as ask by the hub hook.
rows.note: The hook returns ask in ask, ask-when-needed and never-ask alike, and ask beats every allow the hook would add. Claude's dialog cannot carry a class budget, so every classed call asks. Not enforced without a hub hook or under --unattended.

rows.asks: Whether Claude asks before calling the plugin's hub_* MCP tools.
rows.note: unknown: no allow rule for the hub tools was found in the plugin or the launcher. In ask and ask-when-needed Claude's own rules decide. never-ask returns a hook allow for every tool.

rows.asks: Claude's native development-channel confirmation for the hub channel (--dangerously-load-development-channels).
rows.note: Recorded as an attended step when a recovery recreates a Claude session. unknown: whether it appears on every ordinary ahub claude start, and whether Orca profile homes differ.

rows.asks: The person's allow-once through the hub's permission prompt tool, on the console, for a write or shell call of a declared headless implementer.
rows.note: ask asks for every write and shell call. ask-when-needed lets safe project file tools, proven read-only shell commands and bound task commands inside the owned worktree run. There is no never-ask or acceptEdits bypass: never-ask and --unattended are refused at startup. No answer is a denial after approvals.timeout_s. Only a declared headless implementer instance has this form.

rows.asks: The person's allow-once or denial for a publish, external-write, destroy or install call of the headless implementer.
rows.note: The managed hook asks and the current-child-bound prompt tool accepts only a person's allow-once or denial. Not enforced while there is no current managed child.

evidence.needle: no current managed Claude implementer child

rows.asks: None: the implementer's hub tools are an explicit allowed-tools list.
Codex's approval prompts in its TUI for commands, file changes and permission profiles.
rows.note: ask-when-needed sends approval policy on-request on every turn, never-ask sends never so nothing asks, and ask restores the captured native policy once. Received command approval requests are classed by the hub before they reach the TUI. File-change, writeStdin, permission-profile and unreadable requests keep native handling, and native policy can run a call without sending a request. --unattended passes --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox and is refused under a non-ask mode.

rows.asks: The hub console's allow-once or deny, with an optional class budget, for a classed command approval request.
rows.note: The status row says not enforceable: native policy can execute without emitting an approval request, and never-ask sends approvalPolicy never.

evidence.needle: native policy can execute without sending one

rows.asks: Approval requests of the hub-started Codex app-server, answered by whatever is attached to it.
rows.note: unknown: with peers.codex.start_mode headless there is no TUI, and the code gates a classed command request only while a TUI link is open. The mode override (on-request or never) applies to every hub turn/start.

evidence.needle: a hub-made start runs the app-server only

rows.asks: The hub console's allow-once or deny for a classed command approval request, when one is sent.
rows.note: unknown: see codex.tool-approval.headless. Never-ask sends no request at all.

rows.asks: Kimi's own TUI permission prompts.
rows.note: Pull-only: no hub permission mode, busy state, watchdog or console approval. The status row says Kimi approves tools in its own TUI.

evidence.needle: Kimi approves tools and selects its permission mode in its own TUI

rows.asks: Whatever Kimi's own TUI asks. The hub classifies nothing in this form.
Whether Kimi's TUI asks before calling hub_* tools through its project MCP entry.
rows.note: unknown: the TUI's own prompts are not observable by the hub.

rows.asks: ACP session/request_permission, answered on the hub console (ahub permit or the dashboard).
rows.note: ask maps to Kimi default, ask-when-needed to yolo and never-ask to auto. In yolo and auto Kimi sends no request for a call that mode allows, so the hub does not see it. An unanswered request is cancelled as a denial after approvals.timeout_s. ahub up --unattended answers unclassed requests allow-once on its own.

evidence.needle: its native mode ${mode} sends no request for a call it allows

rows.asks: A console prompt titled Action approval with the classes, never auto-approved and without allow_always.
rows.note: Enforced only while the peer's native mode is ask. A request whose payload the agent did not report is not classed. Under --unattended a classed request still waits for a person.

rows.asks: None for the hub's own tools: an exact mcp__agent-hub__<name> title is auto-approved with allow-once only.
ACP permission requests of the headless Qwen, answered on the hub console.
rows.note: ask maps to default, ask-when-needed to auto-edit (file edits run, shell commands ask) and never-ask to yolo, which approves every tool outside any hub sandbox. Qwen is not a start-mode peer: a hub start is headless in every environment, plus a watch pane where a provider exists.

evidence.needle: Modes: ask maps to default, scoped frequency maps to auto-edit

rows.asks: A console prompt titled Action approval with the classes, never auto-approved.
rows.note: Enforced only while the native mode is ask. In auto-edit and yolo Qwen may allow a call without sending a request.

rows.asks: None for the hub's own tools: an exact mcp__agent-hub__<name> title is auto-approved, in the TUI too.
Qwen's can_use_tool request, shown on the hub console. Answering in the Qwen terminal first withdraws the hub's pending approval.
rows.note: Explicit only (ahub qwen --mode tui), never opened by the hub. A hub denial ends the turn without an answer. unknown: whether permission_modes.qwen changes anything for the TUI, which is launched with --approval-mode default.

rows.asks: The same console approval, with the classed title, for a classed call in the dual-output TUI.
Jcode's own native policy. The hub maps no mode for it.
rows.note: permission_modes.jcode is refused by the config loader. In headless form (ACP only) unknown: whether and where Jcode asks, since no hub pre-tool approval path exists.

rows.asks: Nothing from the hub: always-ask is not enforceable for Jcode.

evidence.needle: Jcode still has no hub pre-tool approval path

rows.asks: The hub console's approval at the host permit boundary for each model tool call.
rows.note: ask-when-needed grants write and edit outside native agent configuration paths and proven read-only shell calls, and other shell and git writes ask. never-ask grants each tool once within the existing sandbox and path guard. Two unanswered requests in a row end the turn, never the peer. Pi's own always grant lives only in that start.

evidence.needle: Grant each tool once within the existing sandbox/guard

rows.asks: The hub console's approval for a classed call, checked before never-ask, ask-when-needed or Pi's tool-wide grant.
rows.note: Not enforced for a Pi without a verified live tool bridge. unattended never answers a classed request.

evidence.needle: Pi has no verified live tool bridge

rows.asks: The hub console's approval at the host permit boundary for each model tool call of the hub-native worker.
rows.note: The worker is headless in every environment, so no terminal is involved. The modes behave as for Pi. A local worker offline cannot be enforced.

rows.asks: The hub console's approval for a classed call, checked before any mode grant.
Antigravity's own TUI permission prompts.
rows.note: Pull-only and started only by the person's own ahub agy: conductor starts are refused, so terminal.open and Orca never open it. --dangerously-skip-permissions and --unattended are refused until their native mapping is verified.

evidence.needle: Antigravity approves tools in its own TUI

rows.asks: Whatever Antigravity's own TUI asks. The hub classifies nothing for it.
Whether Antigravity's TUI asks before calling hub_* tools from its project plugin.
rows.note: unknown: not observable by the hub.

rows.asks: Whether the peer asks before calling the hub's own tools.
rows.note: unknown: neither the code nor the docs state it for these kinds. Ask the T0 reviewer or probe it in the T4 receipt.

rows.asks: Nothing when terminal.open is configured. With none, a hub-made TUI start is refused and names the command to run by hand.
rows.note: start_mode headless avoids the terminal. pi.auto_start starts Pi with the hub through the same path.

rows.asks: Nothing when terminal.open is configured. With none, a hub-made Claude start is refused and names the command to run by hand.
rows.note: Claude has no start_mode: its TUI is its only form (a headless implementer is a separately declared instance).

rows.asks: Nothing from the hub: Orca creates the terminal. Native prompts of the peer then appear in that terminal.
rows.note: A configured terminal.open template wins over Orca.

evidence.needle: Orca, when the hub runs in an Orca worktree

rows.asks: Nothing from the hub: Orca creates the terminal. Claude's native prompts then appear in that terminal.
rows.note: Orca runs Claude under per-profile CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR homes (issue #999). ahub setup does not read CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so unknown: whether the hub plugin is installed in each profile home.

rows.asks: A separate console y (or the peer id typed in the dashboard, or --yes in a terminal) before a never-ask mode takes effect.
rows.note: A never-ask default from an untracked config.local.json starts in ask and appears as a pending console question at hub start. There is no boot --yes bypass, and automatic config effects stop at ask-when-needed. Only the person sets a mode: no hub tool or conductor tool can.

evidence.needle: Only its separate console y enables that default

rows.asks: Nothing: an unanswered request is cancelled as a denial after approvals.timeout_s. It decides what an unwatched run does when a prompt appears.

evidence.needle: An unanswered request is cancelled after `approvals.timeout_s`

rows.asks: ahub up --unattended answers unclassed ACP, Pi and local requests allow-once on its own. A classed request and a person-only request are never answered for the person.
rows.note: Per-launch native flags are separate: ahub claude --unattended skips every Claude permission check, hooks included, and ahub codex --unattended is refused under a non-ask mode.

evidence.needle: a classed call is never answered for the person, `--unattended` included

rows.asks: Raising tasks.auto_pull or a permission default needs a settings session (ahub ui --settings) or the person's own terminal. An ordinary dashboard session cannot. The configured conductor may set only thirteen live keys, which include task_sweep.enabled and task_sweep.auto_reassign but not tasks.auto_pull and no permission key.

evidence.needle: can widen what agents do without asking
Only the thirteen existing live registry keys

rows.asks: No person prompt. With tasks.auto_pull off, a freed slot waits until a planner assigns or pulls a card. On, the hub pulls the top explicitly reserved ready card, never an unreserved or PII one.
No person prompt. The idle sweep is off by default. When on with auto_reassign off, it posts notices and a reassignment suggestion and a planner or the person moves the task.

With auto_merge off (the default) the hub merges nothing: the person or the configured conductor runs ahub sdlc merge. On, the guarded merge runs after an approving review at the current head. A release PR always needs the person's consent.
rows.note: The merge argv is a closed shape (squash, match-head-commit), never --admin.

rows.asks: The person's ahub sdlc authorize-release in a person's terminal, and the pre-push guard that fails closed on version tags. Agents and delegated calls cannot authorize.

evidence.needle: Agents and delegated live-test calls cannot authorize
